answer: One concrete mechanism: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because harbor only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
